044/**
045 * Works with a {@link BufferedImage}
046 * in a JScrollPane
047 * and some dynamic configuration Suppliers.
048 * There are some helper method to support hardware acceleration.
049 */
050@SuppressWarnings("serial")
051public class ZoomCanvas extends JPanel {
052  /** Rendering quality. */
053  public enum RenderingQuality { /**high.*/ HIGH, /**medium.*/ MEDIUM, /**low.*/ LOW }
054
055  /** How to handle resize. */
056  public enum ResizeMode {
057    /** Keep the same point centered during resize. */
058    CENTER_PANNING,
059    /** Crop/pad right/bottom edge movement; lock top/left edge movement. */
060    CROP_PAD
061  }
062
063  private final JScrollPane scrollPane;
064  private final DoubleSupplier zoomFactor;
065  private BufferedImage image;
066  private final Supplier<RenderingQuality> quality;
067  private ResizeMode resizeMode = ResizeMode.CROP_PAD; // true for "Other" style.
068
069  /**
070   * Initializes the canvas independently of the parent Application context.
071   * <p>
072   * If quality is hooked to a slider's ValueIsAdjusting, remember
073   * to trigger zoomCanvas.repaint() from the slider's mouseReleased
074   * listener to draw final frame at non-adjusting quality.
075   *
076   * @param scrollPane The container scrollpane used to evaluate live viewport bounds.
077   * @param zoomFactor current zoom lambda (e.g., () -> this.currentZoom)
078   * @param quality rendering quality  lambda
079   */
080  public ZoomCanvas(JScrollPane scrollPane, DoubleSupplier zoomFactor,
081                    Supplier<RenderingQuality> quality) {
082    this.scrollPane = scrollPane;
083    this.zoomFactor = zoomFactor;
084    this.quality = quality;
085    setLayout(null);
086    setupScrollPaneCropPadCenterPanListener();
087  }
088
089  /**
090   *
091   * @param scrollPane
092   * @param zoomFactor
093   */
094  public ZoomCanvas(JScrollPane scrollPane, DoubleSupplier zoomFactor) {
095    this(scrollPane, zoomFactor, () -> RenderingQuality.MEDIUM);
096  }
097
098  /**
099   * Updates the underlying image matrix and forces a canvas layout repaint.
100   * @param newImage
101   */
102  public void setImage(BufferedImage newImage) {
103    this.image = newImage;
104    revalidate();
105    repaint();
106  }
107
108  /**
109   * Gets the active image currently being displayed.
110   * @return
111   */
112  public BufferedImage getCurrentImage() {
113    return this.image;
114  }
115
116  /**
117   * How is resize handled.
118   * @return
119   */
120  public ResizeMode getResizeMode() {
121    return resizeMode;
122  }
123
124  /**
125   * How to handle resize.
126   * @param resizeMode
127   */
128  public void setResizeMode(ResizeMode resizeMode) {
129    this.resizeMode = resizeMode;
130  }
131
132  /**
133   * @return size of zoomed image.
134   */
135  @Override
136  public Dimension getPreferredSize() {
137    Dimension viewSize = scrollPane.getViewport().getSize();
138
139    // If there's no image, fill the viewport space completely
140    if (image == null) {
141      return viewSize;
142    }
143
144    double currentZoom = zoomFactor.getAsDouble();
145    int w = (int) (image.getWidth() * currentZoom);
146    int h = (int) (image.getHeight() * currentZoom);
147
148    return new Dimension(Math.max(w, viewSize.width), Math.max(h, viewSize.height));
149  }
150
151  /**
152   * Paint the zoomed/scaled image.
153   */
154  @Override
155  protected void paintComponent(Graphics g) {
156    // System.err.println("PAINT_COMPONENT zoom " + zoomFactor.getAsDouble());
157    super.paintComponent(g);
158    Graphics2D g2d = (Graphics2D) g.create();
159
160    g2d.setRenderingHint(RenderingHints.KEY_ANTIALIASING, RenderingHints.VALUE_ANTIALIAS_ON);
161
162    // 1. IF NO IMAGE IS SET -> Render centered placeholder text
163    if (image == null) {
164      g2d.setColor(getBackground());
165      g2d.fillRect(0, 0, getWidth(), getHeight());
166
167      //String text = "No Image Loaded. Please Select an Image.";
168      String text = "No Image";
169      g2d.setFont(new Font("SansSerif", Font.BOLD, 16));
170      g2d.setColor(Color.DARK_GRAY);
171
172      FontMetrics metrics = g2d.getFontMetrics(g2d.getFont());
173      int textX = (getWidth() - metrics.stringWidth(text)) / 2;
174      int textY = ((getHeight() - metrics.getHeight()) / 2) + metrics.getAscent();
175
176      g2d.drawString(text, textX, textY);
177      g2d.dispose();
178      return;
179    }
180
181    // Draw scaled image.
182    // May be hardware-accelerated. If ...
183    double currentZoom = zoomFactor.getAsDouble();
184    int imgW = (int) (image.getWidth() * currentZoom);
185    int imgH = (int) (image.getHeight() * currentZoom);
186
187    int x = (getWidth() - imgW) / 2;
188    int y = (getHeight() - imgH) / 2;
189
190    setRenderingHints(g2d);
191
192    g2d.drawImage(image, x, y, imgW, imgH, null);
193    g2d.dispose();
194  }
195
196  private void setRenderingHints(Graphics2D g2d) {
197    switch (quality.get()) {
198      case LOW -> {
199        g2d.setRenderingHint(RenderingHints.KEY_INTERPOLATION,
200                             RenderingHints.VALUE_INTERPOLATION_NEAREST_NEIGHBOR);
201        g2d.setRenderingHint(RenderingHints.KEY_RENDERING, RenderingHints.VALUE_RENDER_SPEED);
202      }
203      case MEDIUM -> {
204        // Fast processing during drag operations
205        g2d.setRenderingHint(RenderingHints.KEY_INTERPOLATION,
206                             RenderingHints.VALUE_INTERPOLATION_BILINEAR);
207        g2d.setRenderingHint(RenderingHints.KEY_RENDERING, RenderingHints.VALUE_RENDER_SPEED);
208      }
209      case HIGH -> {
210        // Pristine rendering when static or clicking buttons
211        g2d.setRenderingHint(RenderingHints.KEY_INTERPOLATION,
212                             RenderingHints.VALUE_INTERPOLATION_BICUBIC);
213        g2d.setRenderingHint(RenderingHints.KEY_RENDERING, RenderingHints.VALUE_RENDER_QUALITY);
214      }
215    }
216  }
217
218  /**
219   * The returned image is a "compatible" image,
220   * {@link GraphicsConfiguration#createCompatibleImage(int, int, int) }
221   *
222   * @param bytes
223   * @return image for the bytes
224   * @throws IOException
225   */
226  public static BufferedImage bytes2image(byte[] bytes) throws IOException {
227    try (InputStream is = new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes);) {
228      BufferedImage bimg = toCompatibleImage(ImageIO.read(is));
229      return bimg;
230    }
231  }
232
233  /**
234   * When you load your image from a file, convert it into a Hardware-Compatible
235   * Image immediately. This caches the image directly inside VRAM (Video RAM),
236   * making g2d.drawImage() run at hardware speed.
237   * <p>
238   * Usage: When loading the file, wrap it: {@snippet :
239   *     originalImage = toCompatibleImage(ImageIO.read(file));
240   * }
241   *
242   * @param image
243   * @return
244   */
245  public static BufferedImage toCompatibleImage(BufferedImage image) {
246    GraphicsConfiguration gc = GraphicsEnvironment.getLocalGraphicsEnvironment()
247                                   .getDefaultScreenDevice()
248                                   .getDefaultConfiguration();
249
250    // Create a canvas customized exactly for the local GPU layout
251    // NOTE: wonder about the volatile versions of createCompatibleImage?
252    BufferedImage compatibleImage
253        = gc.createCompatibleImage(image.getWidth(), image.getHeight(), image.getTransparency());
254
255    Graphics2D g2d = compatibleImage.createGraphics();
256    g2d.drawImage(image, 0, 0, null);
257    g2d.dispose();
258
259    return compatibleImage;
260  }
261
262  /**
263   * Adjust scrollPane so {@code canvasPoint} is centered in JScrollPane.
264   * @param canvasPoint
265   */
266  public void centerViewportOnCanvasPoint(Point canvasPoint) {
267    if (image == null)
268      return;
269
270    JViewport viewport = scrollPane.getViewport();
271    Dimension viewportSize = viewport.getSize();
272
273    // Calculate the target top-left position for the viewport
274    int targetX = canvasPoint.x - (viewportSize.width / 2);
275    int targetY = canvasPoint.y - (viewportSize.height / 2);
276
277    // Bound the values so we don't scroll past the panel borders
278    Dimension canvasSize = getSize(); // The custom JPanel size
279    targetX = Math.max(0, Math.min(targetX, canvasSize.width - viewportSize.width));
280    targetY = Math.max(0, Math.min(targetY, canvasSize.height - viewportSize.height));
281
282    // Apply the new position to the viewport
283    viewport.setViewPosition(new Point(targetX, targetY));
284  }
285
286  /**
287   * Captures the current visual center point of the viewport,
288   * normalized strictly to the underlying image's pixel grid.
289   * @return the image point that is centered in the viewport.
290   */
291  public Point captureImagePointAtViewportCenter() {
292    if (image == null)
293      return new Point(0, 0);
294
295    // 1. Get current physical component sizes
296    int canvasWidth = getWidth();
297    int canvasHeight = getHeight();
298
299    double currentZoom = zoomFactor.getAsDouble();
300    int imgWidth = (int) (image.getWidth() * currentZoom);
301    int imgHeight = (int) (image.getHeight() * currentZoom);
302
303    // 2. Find the padding offsets inside the centered canvas
304    int imageOffsetX = Math.max(0, (canvasWidth - imgWidth) / 2);
305    int imageOffsetY = Math.max(0, (canvasHeight - imgHeight) / 2);
306
307    // 3. Find the visual center point of what the user sees
308    Point viewPos = scrollPane.getViewport().getViewPosition();
309    Dimension viewSize = scrollPane.getViewport().getSize();
310
311    int viewCenterX = viewPos.x + viewSize.width / 2;
312    int viewCenterY = viewPos.y + viewSize.height / 2;
313
314    // 4. Return the normalized coordinate relative to the photo bounds
315    return new Point(viewCenterX - imageOffsetX, viewCenterY - imageOffsetY);
316  }
317
318  private void setupScrollPaneCropPadCenterPanListener() {
319    scrollPane.addComponentListener(new ComponentAdapter() {
320      private Dimension oldViewportSize;
321
322      @Override
323      public void componentResized(ComponentEvent e) {
324        Dimension newViewportSize = scrollPane.getViewport().getSize();
325        try {
326          // Skip if it's the very first initial layout pass or there's no image
327          if (oldViewportSize == null || image == null)
328            return;
329          // Give canvas extender a chance.
330          if (handleResize(e))
331            return;
332
333          // Only calculate if the window size actually changed
334          if (newViewportSize.width == oldViewportSize.width
335              && newViewportSize.height == oldViewportSize.height) {
336            return;
337          }
338
339          switch (resizeMode) {
340            // center-panning calculation
341            case CENTER_PANNING -> recenterViewOnResize(oldViewportSize, newViewportSize);
342            // top-left pinning, bottom-right crop/pad stability calculation
343            case CROP_PAD -> stabilizeImageOnResize(oldViewportSize, newViewportSize);
344          }
345        } finally {
346          oldViewportSize = new Dimension(newViewportSize);
347        }
348      }
349    });
350  }
351
352  /**
353   * Called when a scrollPane component resize occurs.
354   * This can short circuit {@link ResizeMode} for special handling, like bestFit.
355   * @param e the resize event
356   * @return true to finish resize handling, else false continues handling.
357   */
358  protected boolean handleResize(ComponentEvent e) {
359    return false; // continue normal handling.
360  }
361
362  /**
363   * For CropPad
364   * Strip away the dynamic JPanel centering padding, targets the raw image bounds,
365   * and forces the scrollpane to match the anchor precisely.
366   * @param oldViewportSize
367   */
368  private void stabilizeImageOnResize(Dimension oldViewportSize, Dimension newViewportSize) {
369    if (image == null)
370      return;
371
372    // 1. Get current zoom and image specs
373    double currentZoom = zoomFactor.getAsDouble();
374    int imgW = (int) (image.getWidth() * currentZoom);
375    int imgH = (int) (image.getHeight() * currentZoom);
376
377    // 2. Calculate the old centering padding offsets that were active BEFORE the layout refreshes
378    int oldCanvasWidth = Math.max(oldViewportSize.width, imgW);
379    int oldCanvasHeight = Math.max(oldViewportSize.height, imgH);
380    int oldOffsetX = (oldCanvasWidth - imgW) / 2;
381    int oldOffsetY = (oldCanvasHeight - imgH) / 2;
382
383    // 3. Find the exact position of the view relative to the IMAGE'S top-left pixel (0,0)
384    Point currentScrollPos = scrollPane.getViewport().getViewPosition();
385    int relativeImageX = currentScrollPos.x - oldOffsetX;
386    int relativeImageY = currentScrollPos.y - oldOffsetY;
387    //Notice the following is negative of relativeImage[XY] just calculated
388    //Point v = translateCoord(new Point(0, 0), CoordSystem.IMAGE, CoordSystem.VIEWPORT);
389
390    // 4. Calculate what the NEW centering padding offsets WILL BE in the new window dimensions
391    int newCanvasWidth = Math.max(newViewportSize.width, imgW);
392    int newCanvasHeight = Math.max(newViewportSize.height, imgH);
393    int newOffsetX = (newCanvasWidth - imgW) / 2;
394    int newOffsetY = (newCanvasHeight - imgH) / 2;
395
396    // 5. Reconstruct the absolute target scroll position by mapping the relative coordinate back
397    int targetScrollX = relativeImageX + newOffsetX;
398    int targetScrollY = relativeImageY + newOffsetY;
399
400    // 6. Clamp the scroll parameters so they don't break scrollpane maximum boundaries
401    int maxScrollX = newCanvasWidth - newViewportSize.width;
402    int maxScrollY = newCanvasHeight - newViewportSize.height;
403
404    if (targetScrollX < 0)
405      targetScrollX = 0;
406    if (targetScrollY < 0)
407      targetScrollY = 0;
408    if (targetScrollX > maxScrollX)
409      targetScrollX = Math.max(0, maxScrollX);
410    if (targetScrollY > maxScrollY)
411      targetScrollY = Math.max(0, maxScrollY);
412
413    // 7. Snap the viewport position instantly
414    Point finalScrollPos = new Point(targetScrollX, targetScrollY);
415    javax.swing.SwingUtilities.invokeLater(
416        () -> { scrollPane.getViewport().setViewPosition(finalScrollPos); });
417  }
418
419  /**
420   * For CenterPanning.
421   * Determines where the viewport's center used to be, tracks how much the
422   * viewable space grew or shrank, and applies the compensation to the scrollbars.
423   * @param oldViewportSize
424   */
425  private void recenterViewOnResize(Dimension oldViewportSize, Dimension newViewportSize) {
426    if (image == null)
427      return;
428
429    // 1. Get the current top-left scroll position
430    Point currentScrollPos = scrollPane.getViewport().getViewPosition();
431
432    // 2. Find the absolute pixel coordinate that was dead-center in the old window size
433    int oldCenterX = currentScrollPos.x + (oldViewportSize.width / 2);
434    int oldCenterY = currentScrollPos.y + (oldViewportSize.height / 2);
435
436    // 3. Subtract half of the NEW window size to find the new target scroll position
437    // This calculation shifts the scroll window around the locked center point
438    int targetScrollX = oldCenterX - (newViewportSize.width / 2);
439    int targetScrollY = oldCenterY - (newViewportSize.height / 2);
440
441    // 4. Calculate maximum bounds to prevent scrolling out into empty background space
442    int maxScrollX = getWidth() - newViewportSize.width;
443    int maxScrollY = getHeight() - newViewportSize.height;
444
445    // 5. Clamp the values safely within bounds
446    if (targetScrollX < 0)
447      targetScrollX = 0;
448    if (targetScrollY < 0)
449      targetScrollY = 0;
450    if (targetScrollX > maxScrollX)
451      targetScrollX = Math.max(0, maxScrollX);
452    if (targetScrollY > maxScrollY)
453      targetScrollY = Math.max(0, maxScrollY);
454
455    // 6. Update the viewport coordinates immediately
456    Point finalScrollPos = new Point(targetScrollX, targetScrollY);
457    javax.swing.SwingUtilities.invokeLater(
458        () -> { scrollPane.getViewport().setViewPosition(finalScrollPos); });
459  }
460
461  /**
462   * The various coordinate spaces when working with
463   * a scaled image in a scroll pane.
464   */
465  public enum CoordSystem {
466    /**
467     * Screen pixels relative to the top-left (0,0) of the JScrollPane's Viewport window.
468     * This represents the coordinates of your physical application window.
469     */
470    VIEWPORT,
471
472    /**
473     * Screen pixels relative to the top-left (0,0) of the inner scrollable JPanel surface.
474     * This shifts when the scrollbars move.
475     */
476    CANVAS,
477
478    /**
479     * Raw, unscaled pixel coordinates directly mapping onto the underlying
480     * BufferedImage indices (0 to width-1, 0 to height-1).
481     */
482    IMAGE,
483
484    /**
485     * Pixels in the intermediate coordinate matrix *after* g2d.scale() is applied,
486     * but *before* image offsets are applied. Measured in unscaled image units.
487     */
488    SCALED_IMAGE,
489  }
490
491  /**
492   * Translate a point in one coordinate system to the same position
493   * in another coordinate system.
494   * @param fromPoint
495   * @param fromCoordSystem
496   * @param toCoordSystem
497   * @return coordinates of the position in the target coordinate system
498   */
499  public Point translateCoord(Point fromPoint, CoordSystem fromCoordSystem,
500                              CoordSystem toCoordSystem) {
501    // If the systems match, avoid all math.
502    if (fromCoordSystem == toCoordSystem) {
503      return new Point(fromPoint);
504    }
505
506    JPanel panel = this;
507    double currentZoom = zoomFactor.getAsDouble();
508
509    // 1. Get the current scrolling position from the viewport
510    Point scrollPos = scrollPane.getViewport().getViewPosition();
511
512    CoordSystem activeFromSystem = fromCoordSystem;
513
514    // 2. Pre-process: If coming from VIEWPORT, convert it to CANVAS space first
515    double workingPanelX = fromPoint.x;
516    double workingPanelY = fromPoint.y;
517
518    if (activeFromSystem == CoordSystem.VIEWPORT) {
519      workingPanelX += scrollPos.x;
520      workingPanelY += scrollPos.y;
521      // Now treat it as a CANVAS coordinate for the intermediate calculations
522      activeFromSystem = CoordSystem.CANVAS;
523    }
524
525    // 3. Calculate dynamic image-space offsets on the panel
526    int panelWidth = panel.getWidth();
527    int panelHeight = panel.getHeight();
528    int screenImageWidth = (int) Math.round(image.getWidth() * currentZoom);
529    int screenImageHeight = (int) Math.round(image.getHeight() * currentZoom);
530
531    double offsetXInImageSpace = (panelWidth > screenImageWidth)
532                                     ? ((panelWidth - screenImageWidth) / 2.0) / currentZoom
533                                     : 0.0;
534    double offsetYInImageSpace = (panelHeight > screenImageHeight)
535                                     ? ((panelHeight - screenImageHeight) / 2.0) / currentZoom
536                                     : 0.0;
537
538    // 4. Step 1: Normalize everything down to raw unscaled IMAGE coordinates
539    double imageX = 0;
540    double imageY = 0;
541
542    switch (activeFromSystem) {
543      case IMAGE -> {
544        imageX = fromPoint.x;
545        imageY = fromPoint.y;
546      }
547      case SCALED_IMAGE -> {
548        imageX = fromPoint.x - offsetXInImageSpace;
549        imageY = fromPoint.y - offsetYInImageSpace;
550      }
551      case CANVAS -> {
552        double scaledMouseX = workingPanelX / currentZoom;
553        double scaledMouseY = workingPanelY / currentZoom;
554        imageX = scaledMouseX - offsetXInImageSpace;
555        imageY = scaledMouseY - offsetYInImageSpace;
556      }
557    }
558
559    // 5. Step 2: Project out from IMAGE coordinates to the target destination system
560    double targetX = 0;
561    double targetY = 0;
562
563    // If the target is VIEWPORT, we temporarily compute it as a CANVAS coordinate
564    CoordSystem activeToSystem
565        = (toCoordSystem == CoordSystem.VIEWPORT) ? CoordSystem.CANVAS : toCoordSystem;
566
567    switch (activeToSystem) {
568      case IMAGE -> {
569        targetX = imageX;
570        targetY = imageY;
571      }
572      case SCALED_IMAGE -> {
573        targetX = imageX + offsetXInImageSpace;
574        targetY = imageY + offsetYInImageSpace;
575      }
576      case CANVAS -> {
577        double scaledX = imageX + offsetXInImageSpace;
578        double scaledY = imageY + offsetYInImageSpace;
579        targetX = scaledX * currentZoom;
580        targetY = scaledY * currentZoom;
581      }
582    }
583
584    // 6. Post-process: If the user explicitly requested VIEWPORT space,
585    // subtract scroll offsets
586    if (toCoordSystem == CoordSystem.VIEWPORT) {
587      targetX -= scrollPos.x;
588      targetY -= scrollPos.y;
589    }
590
591    return new Point((int) Math.floor(targetX), (int) Math.floor(targetY));
592  }
593}
